 Nuggets keep paying the price for David Adelman's stubbornness with DeMar DeRozan 
 David Adelman can't keep trotting out DeMar DeRozan if DeRozan keeps dragging the team down. By David Decker | Nov 17, 2026, 5:00 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Oct 24, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Nuggets guard DeMar DeRozan (10) during the first half against the New Orleans Pelicans at Ball Arena. Mandatory Credit: Christopher Hanewinckel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We're taught as kids, and even as we grow older, to learn from our mistakes. That's why it's frustrating as a Denver Nuggets fan to see head coach David Adelman continue to make the same mistake game after game. He's been stubborn about changing the rotation, and the more he keeps putting DeMar DeRozan on the court for big minutes, the more the Nuggets keep slipping.
--> We're taught as kids, and even as we grow older, to learn from our mistakes. That's why it's frustrating as a Denver Nuggets fan to see head coach David Adelman continue to make the same mistake game after game. He's been stubborn about changing the rotation, and the more he keeps putting DeMar DeRozan on the court for big minutes, the more the Nuggets keep slipping.
 Many consider Adelman to be a great X's and O's coach. But that doesn't make up for what the data says. And the data keeps saying to give DeRozan less floor time. Fans don't care if he was promised a large role in the offense (he probably was). Fans care about wins and losses, and the losses may not be happening if they just used someone else in his place, like Alpha Diallo.
--> Many consider Adelman to be a great X's and O's coach. But that doesn't make up for what the data says. And the data keeps saying to give DeRozan less floor time. Fans don't care if he was promised a large role in the offense (he probably was). Fans care about wins and losses, and the losses may not be happening if they just used someone else in his place, like Alpha Diallo.
 The data says to get DeRozan off the court
--> The data says to get DeRozan off the court
 The data doesn't lie, and it matches the eye test. DeRozan is like a bullfighter who uses the "Ole" technique to stop opponents. Per Databallr , in 250 minutes with DeRozan on the court, the Nuggets have a 120.9 defensive rating per 100 possessions, against a 113.1 rating in 331 minutes without him. And the issue compounds offensively. The Nuggets have a 121.0 offensive rating with DeRozan off the court, and a 111.3 with him on the floor.

And the issue compounds offensively. The Nuggets have a 121.0 offensive rating with DeRozan off the court, and a 111.3 with him on the floor.
 Clearly, he isn't working out. I was hopeful before the season began that the Nuggets and Nikola Jokic would find a way to get DeRozan to fit. But he hasn't, and he was terrible again in the Nuggets' 117-105 loss to the Phoenix Suns. 
--> Clearly, he isn't working out. I was hopeful before the season began that the Nuggets and Nikola Jokic would find a way to get DeRozan to fit. But he hasn't, and he was terrible again in the Nuggets' 117-105 loss to the Phoenix Suns. 
 In just 14 minutes, DeRozan was a -15 while shooting just 1-for-6 for 2 points. He's scored 7, 8, 9, and 2 over his past four games, and he's shooting just 14.3% from beyond the arc. Plus, the Nuggets have a -9.5 net differential, while Jokic and DeRozan are on the floor together. He's even bogging down Joker!
--> In just 14 minutes, DeRozan was a -15 while shooting just 1-for-6 for 2 points. He's scored 7, 8, 9, and 2 over his past four games, and he's shooting just 14.3% from beyond the arc. Plus, the Nuggets have a -9.5 net differential, while Jokic and DeRozan are on the floor together. He's even bogging down Joker!
 The spacing is bad, and even when DeRozan gets a wide-open look in the corner, he just runs into triple coverage in the mid-range and fires up a clanker. That could be excusable if he played world-class defense, but he doesn't, and that's where Diallo comes in.
--> The spacing is bad, and even when DeRozan gets a wide-open look in the corner, he just runs into triple coverage in the mid-range and fires up a clanker. That could be excusable if he played world-class defense, but he doesn't, and that's where Diallo comes in.
 Alpha Diallo needs to take minutes from DeRozan
--> Alpha Diallo needs to take minutes from DeRozan
 I'm not going to sit here and tell you Diallo is going to solve the offensive spacing issue, but he's a strong driver, and he can hit an open three better than DeRozan's 14.3%, I'm sure. He's a career 36.8% from downtown over his six-year career in Europe.
--> I'm not going to sit here and tell you Diallo is going to solve the offensive spacing issue, but he's a strong driver, and he can hit an open three better than DeRozan's 14.3%, I'm sure. He's a career 36.8% from downtown over his six-year career in Europe.
 However (in a Stephen A. Smith voice), Diallo can absolutely play better defense. I think I've mentioned that a few times when I've written about Diallo. And I'll say it again. He was the EuroLeague's Best Defender last year, and that's what got him his first NBA contract. Even Cameron Johnson called Diallo a "defensive menace" in training camp.
--> However (in a Stephen A. Smith voice), Diallo can absolutely play better defense. I think I've mentioned that a few times when I've written about Diallo. And I'll say it again. He was the EuroLeague's Best Defender last year, and that's what got him his first NBA contract. Even Cameron Johnson called Diallo a "defensive menace" in training camp.
 But Diallo's fallen out of the rotation for some reason. It's time for Adelman to put him back in because the offense probably won't get much worse by making the change, and the defense will certainly improve, giving the Nuggets a better chance to survive the bench minutes and stop losing leads because Jokic and Jamal Murray need a breather.
